description: Existing NCR creation endpoint. This feature adds ONE optional body field, traveler_input_ref, which links the new NCR to a traveler input; every existing field, required-field validation and success response is unchanged (spec FR-006, FR-007, SC-007). It also changes how the 123 fields traveler_id / traveler_input_name / traveler_input_label are treated (see 'deprecated'). See contracts/traveler-input-lookup.json for the resolver's error codes.
authorization: Unchanged for NCR creation. When traveler_input_ref is present the caller must also have at least read access to that traveler (spec FR-008).

traveler_input_ref.description: traveler_id::input_name. Omitted or blank = a standalone NCR exactly as before. When present it is resolved by the server (parse, read access, input exists, traveler active) BEFORE the NCR is created; any failure creates nothing.

deprecated.traveler_id: Still accepted for one release. Combined with traveler_input_name into a synthesized reference and sent through the same resolver. A traveler_id with no traveler_input_name is now a 400 BAD_REFERENCE (an NCR links to an input, not just a traveler).
deprecated.traveler_input_label: Ignored. The label is now taken from the traveler's own form labels, never from the client.

response.success_201: Unchanged: { success: true, ncr: { ncr_number, ncr_id, status, creation_timestamp, originator_id, part_name, part_number }, wbs_notification_matched, message }

errors.validation_400: Unchanged for the existing required fields. Reported first: if any required field is invalid this is returned before the reference is resolved.
errors.bad_reference_400: { success:false, error:'Validation Error', code:'BAD_REFERENCE', message, details:{ traveler_input_ref:[message] } }
errors.traveler_not_found_404: { ..., code:'TRAVELER_NOT_FOUND' } — nonexistent traveler OR no read access (identical)
errors.traveler_not_active_409: { ..., code:'TRAVELER_NOT_ACTIVE' } — evaluated at submission time (spec FR-012)

behaviour_changes: The stored traveler_link.input_label now always comes from the traveler's labels (server-derived).
An NCR can no longer be created linked to a non-active traveler, a traveler the caller cannot read, or an input that does not exist.
Legacy callers that sent traveler_id without an input name now receive 400 instead of an NCR with an input-less link.
notes: lib/ncr-service.js createNcr(data, user, webBaseUrl) keeps its signature: the route passes it the already-resolved { traveler_id, traveler_input_name, traveler_input_label }.
After a traveler-linked NCR is saved, the traveler's stored finishedInput is refreshed (spec FR-017/FR-020).
